primary_full_report.rationale: Six-page primary conference paper presenting a joint optimization formulation, the LARA alternating optimization algorithm, numerical simulations, and conclusions.
primary_full_report.quote: To solve the formulated mixed integer non-linear optimization problem, we employ the alternating optimization approach where we iteratively optimize the DNN layer assignment subproblem, computing resource allocation subproblem, and subchannel and rate allocation subproblem iteratively until convergence.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Simulates a connected multi-UAV network of 10, 15, and 20 UAVs over a 500 m x 500 m area performing collaborative VGG16 inference.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Breaks pre-trained VGG16 into 16 layers and assigns/offloads layers across neighboring connected UAVs while jointly optimizing compute and subchannel/rate allocation.
collaborative_inference.quote: Each UAV initiating the corresponding inference request can perform the computation required by all DNN layers; however, offloading certain DNN layers to neighboring UAVs with abundant compute resources for processing can improve the inference latency.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Provides Python/CVXPY numerical simulations comparing LARA against OULD, HCN, and HCNN across request counts, compute capacities, and UAV counts.
evaluative_evidence.quote: In this section, we present simulation results to assess the achievable performance of LARA framework. Optimization problems were solved with a Python implementation that used CVXPY package.

alignment.rationale: Formulates and solves joint DNN layer-by-layer assignment with radio subchannel, rate, and compute resource allocation across connected UAVs.
alignment.quote: To this end, we formulate the joint DNN layer assignment, radio and computing resource allocation problem as an optimization problem which aims to minimize the total inference latency.

collaborative_inference.quote: Conversely, if task UAVs select a complex model, they initially partition it into several submodels. Each UAV along the communication link then sequentially infers its respective submodel as shown in Fig. 1

evaluative_evidence.quote: We conduct extensive simulations based on real-world UAV trajectory traces to validate the effectiveness of the proposed AMSM algorithm.

records.title: DNN Task Partitioning and Migration Strategies in Multi-UAV-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing

identity_evidence.quote: IEEE INTERNET OF THINGS JOURNAL, VOL. 13, NO. 13, 1 JULY 2026

primary_full_report.rationale: Twelve-page peer-reviewed IEEE journal article detailing system model, SAC-PER with convex optimization subroutine, simulations, and conclusions.
primary_full_report.quote: Section II provides a detailed description of the system model for the DNN-based multi-UAV-assisted MEC and formulates the optimization problem. Section III presents the proposed algorithm framework. Section IV evaluates the performance of the proposed scheme through simulation experiments.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Evaluates a multi-UAV-assisted MEC system with 3 to 7 UAVs serving 10 to 30 users, including inter-UAV task migration and 3-D trajectories.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: Fig. 8 shows the comparison of weighted energy consumption across different numbers of UAVs. As the number of UAVs increases, the average weighted energy consumption decreases.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Partitions pretrained AlexNet, VGG16, and VGG13 models between users and UAVs and migrates remaining DNN layers between UAVs when energy or CPU-load thresholds are reached.
collaborative_inference.quote: An adaptive splitting policy selectively executes computation-intensive DNN layers on UAVs while retaining lightweight layers on users, and a migration mechanism triggered by battery or CPU-load thresholds relocates the remaining subtasks among UAVs in real time.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Simulates the SAC+CVX scheme in Python 3.7 and PyTorch 1.11.0 across three DNN architectures and compares it against seven learning and partitioning baselines.
evaluative_evidence.quote: For the DNN model, we selected the pretrained AlexNet, VGG16, and VGG13 to ensure that the algorithm can still guarantee an efficient segmentation and offloading strategy under different DNN-based tasks.
